title: TypeError
kicker: Python for SDFs · Fix the error
code:
issue_date = "2023-04-12"
issue_year = issue_date[:4]
age = 2026 - issue_year
print(age, "years old")
traceback: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'int' and 'str'

notes.label: TypeError
notes.text: The type of error. An operation got a kind of value it can't work with.

notes.label: unsupported operand type(s) for -
notes.text: The operation that failed: the subtraction on line 3.

notes.label: 'int' and 'str'
notes.text: The two types it got. `2026` is a number (an int), but `issue_year` is text (a str). Slicing a string gives you a string: `"2023"`, not `2023`.

fixes.label: age = 2026 - int(issue_year)
fixes.title: Best fix
fixes.feedback: `int()` turns the text "2023" into the number 2023, so the subtraction works. Output: `3 years old`
fixes.fixed_code:
issue_date = "2023-04-12"
issue_year = issue_date[:4]
age = 2026 - int(issue_year)
print(age, "years old")

fixes.label: age = "2026" - issue_year
fixes.title: Still a TypeError
fixes.feedback: Now both sides are text, and Python can't subtract text from text either. The message changes to 'str' and 'str'.
fixes.fixed_code:
issue_date = "2023-04-12"
issue_year = issue_date[:4]
age = "2026" - issue_year
print(age, "years old")

fixes.label: age = str(2026) + issue_year
fixes.title: The error goes away, but the answer is wrong
fixes.feedback: `+` on two strings glues them together, so this prints `20262023 years old`. To do math, both values need to be numbers.
fixes.fixed_code:
issue_date = "2023-04-12"
issue_year = issue_date[:4]
age = str(2026) + issue_year
print(age, "years old")
